Given the figure above, find the value of $w.$
q-114804.worked_solution:
The two angles marked in the diagram are vertical. Since vertical angles are congruent, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{w}{3}+{30}^{∘} & ={46}^{∘} \\ \frac{w}{3} & ={16}^{∘} \\ w & ={48}^{∘}\end{aligned}

q-74745.name: Question 3
q-74745.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14173512/assets/add18e4afb099c25b56b798ac69b8b02f7cee49949ef02b5971f71ffde0d7e5c.png)

Compute the measures of the shaded angles in the figure above.
q-74745.worked_solution:
The two angles marked in the diagram are vertical. Since vertical angles are congruent, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-{32}^{∘} & =2x+{16}^{∘} \\ 4x-{32}^{∘} & ={16}^{∘} \\ 4x & ={48}^{∘} \\ x & ={12}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we know $x={12}^{∘},$ we can substitute into one of the expressions to calculate the measure of the angles. Let's substitute into the expression $2x+{16}^{∘}:$

$$
2({12}^{∘})+{16}^{∘}={40}^{∘}
$$

Therefore, both angles have a measure of ${40}^{∘}.$

q-114829.name: Question 5
q-114829.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14173512/assets/cafb9f7367b6f0f53a29e13e17f9b6c2cd6b516fa80afd1959842b52e176642c.png)

In the figure above, $∠POQ$ is a straight angle. Find $m∠QOS.$
q-114829.worked_solution:
Since $∠POQ$ is straight, $m∠POQ={180}^{∘}.$ So by the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
m∠QOR+m∠ROP={180}^{∘}.
$$

Substituting the given expressions into the above, we can solve for $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(4w-{7}^{∘})+(6w-{13}^{∘}) & ={180}^{∘} \\ 10w-{20}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 10w & ={200}^{∘} \\ w & ={20}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we know $w={20}^{∘},$ we can calculate $m∠ROP$ as follows:

$$
m∠ROP=6({20}^{∘})-{13}^{∘}={107}^{∘}
$$

Finally, since the angles $∠QOS$ and $∠ROP$ are vertical angles, they have the same measure:

$$
m∠QOS=m∠ROP={107}^{∘}

In the figure above, $∠SOT$ is a straight angle. Find $m∠TOV.$
q-114834.worked_solution:
Since $∠SOT$ is straight, $m∠SOT={180}^{∘}.$ So by the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
m∠SOU+m∠UOT={180}^{∘}.
$$

Substituting the given expressions into the above, we can solve for $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2z+{60}^{∘})+(3z+{10}^{∘}) & ={180}^{∘} \\ 5z+{70}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 5z & ={110}^{∘} \\ z & ={22}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we know $z={22}^{∘},$ we can calculate $m∠SOU$ as follows:

$$
m∠SOU=2({22}^{∘})+{60}^{∘}={104}^{∘}
$$

Finally, since the angles $∠SOU$ and $∠TOV$ are vertical angles, they have the same measure:

$$
m∠TOV=m∠SOU={104}^{∘}
$$

q-26290.worked_solution:
We have two pairs of vertical angles, and we know that vertical angles are congruent and therefore have the same measure. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠1 & =m∠2, \\ m∠3 & =m∠4.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{58}^{∘} & =m∠2, \\ m∠3 & ={122}^{∘}.\end{aligned}

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠3-m∠2 & ={122}^{∘}-{58}^{∘} \\  & ={64}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

We have two pairs of vertical angles, and we know that vertical angles are congruent and therefore have the same measure. So, we have

m∠1=m∠2,m∠3=m∠4.

122∘=m∠2,67∘=m∠4.
